correctness.rationale: The proof reduces every non-codeword trace to the canonical threshold blocks. Same-block twins force at most one omission per block; the two same-side trace comparisons are exactly interval nonemptiness tests; cross-side equality is exactly simultaneous emptiness of an A-prefix and a B-prefix; and the two remaining conditions are precisely domination. The polynomial then counts the choice of the unique omitted vertex in each marked block. The packaged verifier independently enumerates all 511 canonical connected threshold profiles of orders 2 through 10 and all 349,524 vertex subsets, matching 2,104 coefficient positions exactly. Finite verification is explicitly limited to regression testing.

originality.rationale: The claim is an all-set characterization and cardinality enumerator for ordinary locating-domination on threshold graphs. The closest published sources found either prove general/twin-free split-graph bounds, establish hardness on the broader split class, or study the strictly stronger solid/self locating variants. None of the inspected statements implies the five-condition omission theorem or its twin-thick factorization. published-finding corpus semantic searches returned no threshold-graph ordinary locating-domination classification; the closest hits concern stronger locating variants or different graph families.

value.rationale: Threshold graphs are a canonical structured subclass of split graphs, and prior work shows that the stronger solid location-domination parameter is maximized on exactly this class. The ordinary parameter behaves very differently. The theorem gives a complete, checkable description of every ordinary locating-dominating set, determines all cardinality counts, and yields a clean factorization, exact minimum, and exact basis count when no canonical twin block is singleton. This is a natural structural gap rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
